business.primary_problem: The brand sells through marketplaces and retail partners only and wants a DTC store with a distinctive purchase experience.
business.highest_impact_fix: A single-page checkout with the product configurator embedded in it.
growth_goals: Launch in Ireland alongside the UK

offer.name: Ecommerce Scale

multi_currency.evidence: Q3.1.1: GBP and EUR, both transactional (IE auto-converted).

b2b.evidence: Q1.1.4: direct to consumer, no B2B.

integration.evidence: Q8.1.1: Klaviyo only, via its native app — not a counted integration.

figma_design_system.evidence: Q9.1.2 / Q9.1.3: key screens only, no design system.

offer.rationale: Two scope gates are active (markets, multi-currency) and no L trigger applies, so the engagement classifies as M — Ecommerce Scale; delivery is blocked by exit 11.6.

rejected.reason: Rejected: nothing in the answers separates the markets by entity, range or team, so a second store would duplicate every catalogue, theme and app change for no benefit (and requires Shopify Plus — https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/organization-settings/expansion-stores)
Rejected: no market diverges enough to leave the core store
Eligible, but rejected: the client keeps its own tax registrations, so the fees buy nothing it is not already doing

assumptions.about: Which company invoices the customer in each market
assumptions.assumed: All 2 markets sell through the GB entity
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: A second selling entity moves the recommendation towards expansion stores and requires Shopify Plus

assumptions.about: How the range differs by market
assumptions.assumed: The same range everywhere, or a subset of it
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: A deliberately different range in several markets moves the recommendation to hybrid or expansion stores

assumptions.about: Who runs each market day to day
assumptions.assumed: One central team runs every market
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: Local teams with their own release cycle and data are the strongest non-technical argument for separate stores

assumptions.about: Whether the business will hold its own tax registrations
assumptions.assumed: The business keeps its own registrations and Shopify Markets handles duties and taxes
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: A preference for a partner as legal seller makes a merchant of record the cross-border answer

assumptions.about: Where the stock that serves each market sits
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: Stock inside a destination region changes the duties position, the tax schemes available and Managed Markets eligibility

assumptions.about: App requirements that cannot coexist on one store
assumptions.assumed: No market needs an app the others cannot live with (apps are installed store-wide)
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: One incompatible app requirement is enough to force a separate store for that market

open_inputs.why_it_matters: Which company invoices in each market decides between one store and separate stores, and whether Shopify Plus is required
A deliberately different range per market is the difference between a market catalog and a second store
Local teams that publish independently need separated admins and release cycles
Decides whether the client stays the seller of record or hands that to a partner
Where stock sits changes duties, tax schemes and Managed Markets eligibility

conditions.condition: The business is based in the continental United States, or is an eligible store in Canada or the United Kingdom
The store is on the Basic plan or higher
At least one fulfilment location in the home country
conditions.evidence: No fulfilment countries recorded — assumed to be the home country

conditions.condition: No B2B orders — "B2B orders aren't supported by Managed Markets"
No subscriptions — "Managed Markets doesn't support subscriptions"
No multiple business entities — "Managed Markets doesn't support multiple business entities"

cost_signal.basis: 3.25% Managed Markets fee + 1.5% currency conversion, on top of Shopify Payments processing (https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/international/managed-markets/overview)

items.detail: Fully custom checkout UI — not possible on Shopify (checkout.liquid is retired; only Checkout Extensibility)

More than one market AND the topology inputs are materially unresolved: more than one legal entity recorded with no per-market entity mapping, or the assortment relationship per market unknown, or the invoicing and tax-registration footprint unknown. Fires on missing facts, not on a missing decision — the engine still recommends a topology.
items.destination: Market topology and legal-entity mapping workshop before the solution architecture is baselined.
items.evidence: Topology recommended as single_store_markets at confidence to_validate — the range per market is unknown

assumptions.statement: The client may accept a Checkout Extensibility design if the configurator moves to the product page.
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: The engagement leaves the Liquid offers and routes to a composable platform.

/checkout/customisation.note: Confirmed twice in the discovery call.
